channel.title: Crypto Bulletin
channel.description: Crypto Bulletin reports crypto news on bitcoin, ethereum, stablecoins, exchanges, DeFi protocols, regulation, security incidents and market structure.

item.title: Move Collateral Before a Lending Top-Up
item.description: Move collateral before a lending top-up by checking the loan’s health factor, bridging the right asset, and allowing for settlement and price changes.

item.title: Why Wallet Bridges Can Cost More Than Exchange Withdrawals
item.description: A wallet bridge can cost more because it pays for on-chain execution and cross-chain settlement, while an exchange may set a separate withdrawal price.

item.title: Check TRX and Token Balances Before a Swap
item.description: Compare the token balance, spendable TRX and quoted output before signing; the gap between wallet totals and swap costs shows what the trade will use.

item.title: TRON USDT transfers need TRX for network resources
item.description: TRON charges for USDT transfers through Bandwidth and Energy; learn when TRX is burned, how staking or delegation covers fees, and what senders should check.

item.title: Monero bridge wait times: what to check before sending XMR
item.description: Monero bridge waits include XMR confirmations and bridge processing; check the route’s confirmation threshold and status before sending, since total time varies.

item.title: ZeroFi lists zXMR contract for Sepolia wallet checks
item.description: To verify zXMR on Sepolia, match its contract address and chain ID, inspect the explorer record, then import the address; a wallet label alone proves nothing.

item.title: Bridge first or swap across chains? Choose by the asset you need
item.description: Bridge first when you need the same token on another chain; swap across chains when you want a different asset, weighing fees, slippage and execution risk.

item.title: Fermi swap Routes Explain How Lock-and-Mint Transfers Work
item.description: A lock-and-mint route holds an asset on its source chain and issues a representation on another; choosing one means checking tokens, fees and the return path.

item.title: Why Ethereum deposits wait for confirmations
item.description: Ethereum deposits wait while exchanges verify chain inclusion and risk; blocks arrive about every 12 seconds, but protocol finality takes about 15 minutes.

item.title: ERC-20 bridge approvals depend on the allowance left
item.description: You usually approve a token once per bridge spender, but the allowance may run out, differ by network or remain active after the transfer finishes.

item.title: What a pending cross-chain transfer actually means
item.description: A pending cross-chain transfer has started on its source chain but may still need finality, message verification, delivery and destination execution before funds arrive.

item.title: Cross-chain limit orders should wait for destination funds
item.description: A cross-chain limit order can hold a destination swap until its price clears, but bridge delay, expiry and failed execution shape what the user receives.

item.title: How to set slippage for a Rango Bridge route
item.description: Rango slippage is the maximum output shortfall allowed before a swap fails; set it against route liquidity and volatility, then check minimum received and fees.

item.title: How to Pay a Merchant on Another Blockchain
item.description: Cross-chain merchant payments require the right asset on the requested network; learn when to bridge, when to swap, and how to verify the payment arrived.

item.title: Rango bridge routes balance fees and confirmation time
item.description: Rango Bridge routes swaps across chains, while transfer cost and wait depend on gas, liquidity and network finality; compare the full route against your deadline.

item.title: Why BSC swap quotes differ from chart prices
item.description: A BSC chart shows a recorded market price; a swap quote estimates your route, trade size, fees and slippage, so the two can differ without either being wrong.

item.title: How to Review Token Prices Around PooCoin Buys
item.description: A PooCoin buy screen shows an estimate; compare the pool quote with the transaction receipt, token units and timing to judge the price actually paid.

item.title: Why Ethereum Congestion Delays Layer 2 Deposits
item.description: Ethereum deposits to layer 2s can wait in mainnet’s fee market before bridge messages reach the rollup; transaction status shows which step is holding funds.

item.title: Five checks before choosing a bridge or exchange withdrawal
item.description: Before moving tokens, compare networks, asset contracts, fees, limits, settlement time and recovery options; the cheapest route is not always the safest fit.

item.title: Mantle Treasury Withdrawals Need an Ethereum Claim Plan
item.description: Mantle withdrawals require an L2 transaction, a wait for Ethereum settlement and a separate L1 claim, so treasuries should budget time and gas at both ends.
